::: {.callout-note}
## Purpose

This document describes the recommended fitting strategy when four rotors
produce moving harmonic combs. Their fundamental-frequency trajectories are
known approximately from telemetry. Harmonics from different rotors can become
close and can cross.

The goal is not only to reconstruct the mean spectrum. The fitted model must
also generate the correct shared phase motion within each comb, independent
residual phase motion at each harmonic, multichannel spatial structure, and
behaviour through frequency crossings.
:::

:::: {.callout-important}
## Status

This is the **general strategy and future-complexity** document for the
revised rotor-noise phase family, reconciled to the frozen campaign contracts
(2026-09-13). **C2** — the current implemented candidate — is a strict and
smaller subset of what follows. It is defined in §1 and recorded, together with
the frozen acceptance criteria and the round ledger, in
`docs/experiments/revised-phase-campaign.qmd`. The companion derivations are in
`docs/explainers/bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd`.

Sections marked **optional future** are deliberately not the default: one
scientifically motivated complexity is added only when a **named** acceptance
criterion has actually failed. Round 1 C1 is rejected at planted preflight; C2
is implemented and remote-preflighted, while real DREGON/Michael fitting and
frozen evaluation are running elsewhere and are not results in this document.
:::::

# 1. Main recommendation

Treat the recording as the output of four telemetry-anchored latent
oscillators. Fit isolated regions first. Fit overlapping lines jointly. Use the
complete harmonic family and all microphones to preserve rotor identity through
crossings.

Do not treat the problem as four independent spectral fits. Do not assign a
time-frequency bin permanently to its nearest predicted line. Both approaches
discard the information needed at a crossing.

The fitting pipeline for the **general family** is:

1. Integrate **raw** telemetry to obtain nominal phase trajectories.
2. Estimate telemetry/audio delay and a per-clip frequency bias from isolated,
   high-SNR harmonics.
3. Estimate amplitude profiles and multichannel spatial signatures away from
   crossings.
4. Estimate shared shaft dynamics and independent harmonic diffusion from
   cross-harmonic phase increments — as **initializers and diagnostics only**.
5. *(optional future)* Construct time-dependent groups of overlapping harmonic
   tracks.
6. *(optional future)* Run joint complex-valued state smoothing inside each
   overlap group.
7. Fit powers and the stochastic floor against the frozen overlap-aware
   spectral composite risk.
8. *(optional future)* Refine all parameters jointly from the staged solution.
9. Validate by round-trip simulation, including simulated crossings.

**C2, which is what is actually implemented, is much smaller.** Write $g$ for
the **rig** index — Michael's rig, DREGON, the bench — and $r$ for a rotor
inside that rig. Its whole pipeline is:

1. Integrate **raw** telemetry. No refined or posterior label enters the fit.
2. Fit one delay $\delta_r$ and one per-clip bias $b_{c,r}$ — a random effect
   with a proper prior and a population/recording mean.
3. Initialize amplitudes and spatial signatures away from crossings.
4. Treat complex harmonic phase-increment moments as **diagnostics only**.
   Round 1 C1 tried to use them as production hyperparameter initializers and
   was rejected at honest planted preflight `python-e25ee9`; the earlier
   `python-c049cf` pass was an invalid scalar-zero fixture.
5. Fix $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ as an explicit reference
   assumption, not measured controller physics.
6. **Stage 1:** fit the training marginal expected periodogram for positive
   $\sigma_g$, scalar $D_g$, existing line and floor powers, tied speed law,
   clip bias terms and population bias. The integrated OU state is integrated
   once; there is no state-path optimization and no innovation prior in this
   stage.
7. **Stage 2:** freeze Stage 1 globals and fit per-clip bias plus the dense-grid
   shared $\theta_r/\nu_r$ path as a conditional MAP diagnostic, using the
   residual kernel $\exp(-D_g|\tau|)$ and one exact OU state prior.
8. Divide the relevant composite objective by the frozen scalar **composite
   temperature** $T$, with fixed seed/draw support and loud failure on
   non-positive or non-finite calibration terms.

Its complexity budget is two fitted rig dynamic scale parameters
($\sigma_g$, $D_g$), one fixed reference $\lambda$, one shared carrier family,
ordinary Adam, and two labelled estimator stages. Nothing else is added unless
a **named** acceptance criterion fails. C2 obeys both prohibitions above
trivially: it sums all components continuously and never assigns a bin to a
line.

# 2. Generative model

## 2.1 Telemetry-guided nominal phase

Let $\widehat f_r(t)$ be the measured fundamental frequency, in hertz, of rotor
$r\in\{1,2,3,4\}$. Its nominal phase is

$$
\widehat\Phi_r(t)
=2\pi\int_0^t\widehat f_r(s)\,ds.
$$

The actual carrier is not assumed to equal telemetry exactly. The identifiable
parameterization has exactly three parts: a time offset $\delta_r$, a per-clip
frequency bias $b_{c,r}$, and **one** stochastic residual:

$$
\boxed{
\Phi_r(t)
=2\pi\int_0^t
\left[
f_{\text{raw},r}(s-\delta_r)+b_{c,r}
\right]ds
+\theta_r(t),
}
$$

equivalently, in instantaneous-frequency form,

$$
f_{\text{actual},r}(t)
=f_{\text{raw},r}(t-\delta_r)+b_{c,r}+\frac{\nu_r(t)}{2\pi}.
$$

Here $f_{\text{raw},r}$ is the **raw** published telemetry array. The refined
or posterior trajectory is fit provenance and a diagnostic — never an input to
the primary fit, and never a scoring reference. The bias $b_{c,r}$ is a
per-clip random effect with a proper prior and a population/recording mean, not
a free per-clip number. The gauge is fixed: $\theta_r(t_0)=0$, the initial
$\nu_r$ is drawn from its stationary distribution, and the mean OU is
stationary-zero in law. There is **no** second per-frame carrier correction
and no calibration spline (§9).

The time offset is important. A small telemetry/audio misalignment creates a
systematic phase error when the rotor accelerates. The error grows with
harmonic order.

## 2.2 Shared shaft dynamics

For each rotor, let the residual angular-frequency error be OU:

$$
d\nu_r(t)
=-\lambda_r\nu_r(t)\,dt
+\sqrt{2\lambda_r\sigma_{\nu,r}^2}\,dW_r^{(0)}(t),
$$

and let

$$
d\theta_r(t)=\nu_r(t)\,dt.
$$

All harmonics of rotor $r$ share $\theta_r(t)$. Different rotors initially have
independent shaft states.

For C2 these are rig-level except for the fixed reference time scale:
$\lambda_r\equiv\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and
$\sigma_{\nu,r}\equiv\sigma_g$, with $\sigma_g$ one fitted positive number for
all four rotors of rig $g$ (§1). The time-resolved object fitted in Stage 2 is
the state path itself, after Stage 1 globals are frozen. The fixed $\lambda$ is
reported as a reference assumption — never as a measured value.

## 2.3 Independent harmonic phase diffusion

Each order has an additional source-side residual:

$$
d\epsilon_{rk}(t)
=\sqrt{2D_{rk}}\,dW_{rk}(t).
$$

For **C2** this too is one scalar per **rig**: $D_{rk}\equiv D_g$ for every
rotor $r$ and order $k$. $D_g$ is fitted in Stage 1, frozen for Stage 2, and is
shared across every order **and** every microphone, because $\epsilon$ is
source-side; its units are phase rad$^2$/s, and there is **no hidden $k$
scaling**. Per-order $D_{rk}$, any order law, and the hierarchy
$\log D_{rk}=d_0+d_1\log k+u_k$ are optional future complexity, admitted only
on evidence.

Each harmonic's **initial** residual phase is drawn **uniform on $[0,2\pi)$**,
independently per harmonic and shared across microphones. This is a
requirement rather than a matter of taste, but the reason is **not** the
increment kernel: a deterministic $\epsilon_{rk}(0)$ cancels in
$\epsilon_{rk}(t)-\epsilon_{rk}(s)$, so the increment kernel is
$\exp(-D_g|t-s|)$ whatever the initial condition. The reason is that uniform
initial phases make every phasor **zero-mean**, which is what cancels the
cross-harmonic and cross-component expectation terms in the summed powers and
removes any deterministic-carrier mean component
(`bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd` §2.2). With $\epsilon_{rk}(0)=0$ those
cross-terms survive and the predicted spectrum stops matching what the
renderer produces.

The phase of order $k$ is

$$
\boxed{
\phi_{rk}(t)
=k\Phi_r(t)+\epsilon_{rk}(t).
}
$$

The acoustic signal at microphone $m$ is

$$
x_m(t)
=\operatorname{Re}\left\{
\sum_{r=1}^4\sum_k
a_{mrk}(t)e^{i\phi_{rk}(t)}
\right\}
+u_m(t),
$$

where $a_{mrk}(t)$ is a slowly varying complex transfer coefficient and
$u_m(t)$ is the stochastic floor.

If $\epsilon_{rk}$ represents source-side acoustic generation, the same
$\epsilon_{rk}(t)$ must be used at all microphones. Microphone-side or
propagation phase noise, if later required, must be introduced as a separate
process.

# 3. What a crossing means

A crossing occurs when

$$
k\widehat f_r(t)\approx l\widehat f_s(t)
$$

for two distinct components $(r,k)$ and $(s,l)$.

Their frequencies may coincide, but their identities do not. Identity remains
attached to:

- the telemetry trajectory before and after the crossing;
- the other harmonics belonging to the same rotor;
- the shared shaft state of that rotor;
- its spatial transfer vector across microphones;
- its slowly varying amplitude profile.

At one exact crossing, one microphone and one Fourier coefficient cannot
identify two arbitrary complex sources. The full trajectory can still be
identifiable because information exists before, during, and after the crossing.

The fit must therefore smooth through crossings. It must not make an
independent source-assignment decision in every STFT cell.

C2's crossing policy follows from exactly that, and it needs no new machinery:

- unresolved overlaps are **excluded from moment diagnostics**, with the
  isolation and SNR gates declared before any estimate;
- the conditional spectral model **sums all components continuously**, so a
  crossing remains a set of **shared latent states** rather than a set of
  independent nearest-bin labels;
- no allocation is forced when a pair is genuinely unidentifiable — the
  uncertainty, or the unresolved group, is reported instead (§8.3).

# 4. Observation representation

## 4.1 Retain complex observations

Use complex analytic subbands or the complex STFT. Do not reduce the data to
periodogram power before estimating phase dynamics and source identity.

For a local time-frequency region, write

$$
\mathbf Y_{nq}
=\sum_{(r,k)\in\mathcal C_{nq}}
\mathbf h_{rk,q}
A_{rk,n}
G_{rk,nq}
e^{i[k\theta_{r,n}+\epsilon_{rk,n}]}
+\boldsymbol\eta_{nq}.
$$

Here:

- $\mathbf Y_{nq}\in\mathbb C^M$ contains all microphones;
- $\mathcal C_{nq}$ contains the lines that overlap cell $(n,q)$;
- $\mathbf h_{rk,q}$ is the multichannel spatial signature;
- $A_{rk,n}\ge0$ is the source amplitude;
- $G_{rk,nq}$ is a telemetry-derived window or chirp atom;
- $\boldsymbol\eta_{nq}$ contains floor and modelling error.

## 4.2 Telemetry-derived atoms

For time-varying carriers, do not approximate every frame by a static sinusoid
at its centre frequency unless the within-frame motion is negligible.

For window $w_n(t)$, construct

$$
G_{rk,n}(f)
=\int w_n(t)
\exp\!\left\{
i k\widehat\Phi_r(t)-i2\pi ft
\right\}dt.
$$

This atom contains the actual:

- frequency trajectory inside the frame;
- fractional-bin offset;
- analysis window;
- harmonic-order scaling.

The stochastic residual phases then modulate this nominal atom.

:::: {.callout-warning}
## The latent path is integrated inside the atom, never evaluated at its centre

The nominal atom $G_{rk,n}$ above carries the *telemetry* motion inside the
frame. It is **not** sufficient to multiply it by one frame-level residual
$\exp\{i(k\theta_{r,n}+\epsilon_{rk,n})\}$: that factorisation is exact only if
the residual phase is constant across the entire window. Counterexample:
$\theta(t)=a\sin(2\pi t/T)$ and $\theta(t)=0$ agree at both frame boundaries
and frame centres, yet

$$
\int w(t)\exp\left\{ik\theta(t)-i2\pi ft\right\}dt
$$

differs between them. **Overlapping frames do not recover the missing subwindow
dynamics**, because overlapping frames re-use the same samples.

The conditional observation mean is therefore

$$
\boxed{
\mu_{mnq}
=\sum_{r,k} h_{mrk,q}
\sum_{j\in\text{window}(n)} w_{nj}A_{rk,j}\,
\exp\!\left\{i\left[
k\Phi_{0,rj}+k\theta_{rj}+\epsilon_{rkj}-2\pi f_qt_j
\right]\right\},
}
$$

with the latent path evaluated **inside** the sum. Amplitude changes inside a
ramp enter the atom $a_j=w_{nj}A_{rk,j}$ too. Frame-mean speed, a frame-centre
phase multiplier, a broaden-by-slope rule and a chirp-width heuristic are all
excluded for moving carriers.
::::

## 4.3 Prefer heterodyned subbands for state fitting

The full audio-rate likelihood is expensive. A practical compromise is to
extract narrow complex subbands around predicted harmonic trajectories.

For each candidate component:

1. heterodyne by $e^{-ik\widehat\Phi_r(t)}$;
2. low-pass filter to a band wide enough to contain carrier error, physical
   linewidth, and nearby crossings;
3. downsample to a rate that resolves the fastest expected phase dynamics;
4. retain all components jointly when their extraction bands overlap.

This produces a much smaller complex time series while preserving the phase
information needed by the state-space model.

## 4.4 The state grid, and what the observation array cannot be

Two constraints follow from this representation, and both are easy to get
wrong.

**The state grid is set by the dynamics, not by the spectral window.** Put
$(\theta,\nu)$ — and $\epsilon$, if it is ever represented explicitly — on a
grid chosen from the fastest phase bandwidth, **independently** of the STFT
window and hop. Overlap between analysis frames does not resolve subwindow
dynamics (§4.2).

:::: {.callout-warning}
## Interpolating between grid points omits the OU bridge variance

Conditioning only on dense-grid MAP endpoints and interpolating between them
**omits the integrated-OU bridge variance** between those points. Call that a
**grid approximation**, and demonstrate convergence as $\Delta_{\text{state}}$
shrinks at fixed STFT hop and window. Including an exact Gaussian bridge
covariance in the kernel would remove the approximation, and is optional future
complexity. Neither choice forces full complex smoothing.
::::

**A redundant complete STFT has a singular covariance.** Propagate the floor
covariance through the same linear analysis operator $A$: for a redundant
complete STFT, $\operatorname{Cov}(Y)=A\Sigma_uA^{H}$ is singular, because
$\operatorname{rows}(A)>\operatorname{rank}(A)$. An exact Gaussian likelihood
would therefore have to operate on a non-redundant support or on its true
singular support; otherwise the complex objective is a **composite** and must
be labelled one. Plant the sinusoidal subwindow path and the duplicate-window
rank-deficiency case.

# 5. Dynamic covariance and initial parameter estimates

## 5.1 Phase-increment covariance within a rotor

After removing nominal telemetry phase, define

$$
\psi_{rk}(t)=k\theta_r(t)+\epsilon_{rk}(t).
$$

For lag $\tau$,

$$
\operatorname{Cov}
\left[\Delta\boldsymbol\psi_r(\tau)\right]
=V_{\theta,r}(\tau)\mathbf k\mathbf k^T
+2|\tau|\operatorname{diag}(D_{r1},\ldots,D_{rK}),
$$

where

$$
V_{\theta,r}(\tau)
=2\sigma_{\nu,r}^2
\left[
\frac{|\tau|}{\lambda_r}
-\frac{1-e^{-\lambda_r|\tau|}}{\lambda_r^2}
\right].
$$

The off-diagonal terms contain only shared shaft motion:

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\Delta\psi_{rk},\Delta\psi_{rl})
=klV_{\theta,r}(\tau),
\qquad k\ne l.
$$

Estimate $\lambda_r$ and $\sigma_{\nu,r}$ primarily from these off-diagonal
terms. Then estimate $D_{rk}$ from the diagonal residuals.

These moment estimates are **initializers and diagnostics only**. They never
enter the fit as a second likelihood factor, and no separate phase loss is
stacked on the spectral objective: the same phase-track data added twice would
count the same observations, and the same integrated state covariance, as
independent evidence. The pooling itself is done by diagonal or generalised
least squares, which is an **approximation** — the pair estimates share shaft
increments, share an order whenever two pairs overlap, and share overlapping
time windows — so quote uncertainty from contiguous-block variation (a
moving-block bootstrap over whole blocks), never from a pair count. A negative
raw estimate is an **observation**, neither an impossible logarithm nor a zero.

## 5.2 Order-normalised differences

For two orders from the same rotor,

$$
\frac{\psi_{rk}}{k}-\frac{\psi_{rl}}{l}
=\frac{\epsilon_{rk}}{k}-\frac{\epsilon_{rl}}{l}.
$$

The shaft cancels. Under independent Wiener residuals,

$$
\operatorname{Var}\!\left[
\Delta\left(
\frac{\psi_{rk}}{k}-\frac{\psi_{rl}}{l}
\right)
\right]
=2|\tau|
\left(
\frac{D_{rk}}{k^2}+\frac{D_{rl}}{l^2}
\right).
$$

Use this as both an initializer and a model check. Nonlinear growth in lag means
that the independent residual is not well described by Wiener phase.

## 5.3 Cross-rotor covariance

The initial model predicts zero process covariance between different rotors.
Estimate cross-rotor phase-increment covariance away from frequency crossings.
Non-zero structure may indicate:

- a shared power-supply or controller process;
- structural vibration coupled across arms;
- common propagation effects;
- telemetry errors;
- leakage between extracted subbands.

Only add a shared cross-rotor state if this covariance persists after leakage
and carrier calibration have been controlled.

# 6. Time-dependent overlap groups — optional future

::::: {.callout-warning}
## C2 builds no groups at all

The overlap **graph** of §6.1 and the temporal **hysteresis** of §6.2 are
demoted to **optional future** complexity. C2's conditional spectral model sums
**all** components continuously, so a crossing is merely an interval in which
two terms of one sum coincide in frequency; it is not a set of components to be
grouped, tracked and assigned. Unresolved overlaps are excluded from moment
diagnostics, and nothing else changes. Heterodyned phase extraction may reuse
the existing tools for diagnostics; no new generic crossing machinery is built,
and no nearest-component assignment is ever made. The physical principle of
§6.3 — couple a crossing to the rotor's other harmonics — is exactly what C2
realises by sharing one latent shaft state.
:::::

## 6.1 Optional future: build an overlap graph

At every time block, create one node for each visible component $(r,k)$.
Connect two nodes when their predicted observation supports overlap.

A conservative overlap threshold is

$$
B_{rk,n}
:=B_{\mathrm{window},n}
+B_{\mathrm{physical},rk}
+B_{\mathrm{telemetry},rk,n}
+B_{\mathrm{margin}}.
$$

Connect $(r,k)$ and $(s,l)$ when

$$
|k\widehat f_r(n)-l\widehat f_s(n)|
<B_{rk,n}+B_{sl,n}.
$$

Every connected component of this graph would then be fitted jointly. Most
components contain one line, and only local regions around crossings would
require multi-source inference. This is machinery that a continuous sum does
not need.

## 6.2 Optional future: add temporal hysteresis

If groups ever exist, do not create and destroy them at one-frame boundaries.
Extend every crossing group several correlation times before and after the
detected overlap, so that a smoother sees separated observations on both sides
of the ambiguous interval. The extension should cover at least

$$
\max\left(
1/\lambda_r,
1/\lambda_s,
\text{several phase-observation frames}
\right).
$$

## 6.3 Couple a crossing to other harmonics

A local pairwise crossing fit can still be ambiguous. Include evidence from
other reliable orders of both rotors through their shared shaft states.

It is not necessary to include every spectral bin in one dense observation
matrix. The state for $\theta_r$ can be informed by non-crossing harmonic
subbands while a small observation group handles the actual collision.

# 7. Staged fitting procedure

C2's staging is deliberately short and explicitly labelled. Stage 0 fixes the
conventions. Stage 1 fits marginal global parameters with the OU state
integrated out once. Stage 2 freezes those globals and fits conditional carrier
tracks as diagnostics. Stages 4, 5, 6 and 8 are retained below as **optional
future** complexity.

::::: {.callout-important}
## The two C2 stages are not one evidence calculation

Stage 1 and Stage 2 are two estimator stages, not exact EM and not two
independent likelihood factors. Stage 1 optimizes a valid marginal
mean-prediction composite risk. Stage 2 is a plug-in conditional MAP diagnostic
under frozen globals. Do not add their final objectives as Bayesian evidence,
and do not claim marginal spectra identify shared causal shaft motion.
:::::

## Stage 0: preprocessing and frozen conventions

The observation conventions are frozen before anything is fitted:

- the existing **16 kHz** convention;
- **periodic Hann**, $N_{\text{FFT}}=16384$, **hop 1024** (64 ms);
- fixed band **30--7900 Hz** — never lowered to conceal filter loss;
- fixed microphones;
- one resampling path for real and rendered audio;
- an exactly defined analytic-signal / STFT normalization, and a stored phase
  convention for every telemetry-derived atom.

Then, before optimizing the physical model:

1. Align audio channels and telemetry clocks approximately.
2. Mark steady, accelerating, low-SNR, clipped, and missing-telemetry regions.
3. Declare the missing/weak-order and SNR/isolation gates **before** any
   estimate is computed.
4. Detect candidate harmonic crossings with a deliberately wide margin, and use
   that detection only to **exclude** unresolved overlaps from moment
   diagnostics.

Do not silently interpolate long telemetry gaps. Treat the carrier as more
uncertain in those intervals.

## Stage 1: delay and per-clip bias — and nothing else

Estimate $\delta_r$ and the per-clip bias $b_{c,r}$ from isolated high-SNR
harmonics, fitting several orders simultaneously. **There is no calibration
spline** (§9): the only time-resolved carrier object is the shaft state.

For candidate calibration parameters, examine the residual phase

$$
\rho_{rk}(t)
=\arg Y_{rk}(t)
-k\widehat\Phi_r(t-\delta_r)
-2\pi kb_{c,r}t,
$$

where $\widehat\Phi_r$ integrates the **raw** telemetry. A correct telemetry
correction is shared across orders after division by $k$. Choose $\delta_r$ and
$b_{c,r}$ to minimize the shared systematic residual curvature, not the error
of one harmonic alone.

Use a robust loss or exclude crossings during this stage. A wrong time offset
can otherwise be absorbed into $\theta_r$ and falsely inflate the fitted OU
variance; conversely a constant rate error leaves a $k$-proportional drift that
mimics shaft motion exactly. Report finite-record bias and slow-OU
confounding — never repair them with a second free path.

## Stage 2: amplitude and spatial initialization

Use non-overlapping regions to estimate:

- the order power profiles $P_{rk}(c_r)$;
- smooth amplitude changes over time;
- the complex microphone vector $\mathbf h_{rk}$;
- floor cross-spectral covariance $\mathbf\Sigma_F(f,n)$.

Normalise the spatial vector to remove scale ambiguity, for example

$$
\|\mathbf h_{rk}\|_2=1,
$$

and store total power in $P_{rk}$. Fix one phase convention for
$\mathbf h_{rk}$ so that propagation phase does not exchange arbitrarily with
the latent source phase.

Regularise spatial signatures smoothly across frequency or harmonic order when
the array physics supports it. Do not allow them to jump during crossings.

## Stage 3: phase-dynamics diagnostics

On high-SNR, non-crossing intervals, the moment machinery can still:

1. extract residual harmonic phases from the complex subbands;
2. compute the increment covariance at several lags;
3. inspect whether off-diagonal covariance follows the harmonic-order loading;
4. inspect order-normalised differences.

These moment estimates are **diagnostics only**. They do not re-enter the fit as
a second likelihood factor, and no separate phase loss is stacked on the
spectral objective. Round 1 C1 used them as production hyperparameter
initializers and was rejected at honest planted preflight `python-e25ee9`. The
earlier `python-c049cf` pass was an invalid scalar-zero fixture.

The moment implementation remains useful for diagnostics: the off-diagonal
$\operatorname{Cov}/(kl)$ treatment, exact nominal integrated heterodyne and
valid time-pair alignment / per-frame isolation are implemented in
`revised_phase.estimate_shaft_dynamics` (integrated raw heterodyne, per-frame
isolation, common-pair covariance). But C2 does **not** use it to set
$\lambda_g$ or $\sigma_g$: $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ is fixed
by assumption, and $\sigma_g,D_g$ are fitted in the Stage 1 marginal
periodogram objective.

If a named acceptance failure later demands per-order diffusion, the order law

$$
\log D_{rk}
:=d_{0,r}+d_{1,r}\log k+u_{rk},
\qquad
u_{rk}\sim N(0,\sigma_{D,r}^2),
$$

is available as **optional future** complexity. There is no conjugate closed
form for it, and moment estimates supply diagnostics only, never an objective.

## C2 Stage 1 and Stage 2: marginal fit, then conditional carrier diagnostic

Stage 1 fits $\sigma_g,D_g$, line powers, floor, tied speed law, clip bias terms
and the population bias from the training marginal expected periodogram with
$\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ fixed. The integrated OU state is
integrated out once; there is no optimized state path and no innovation-prior
energy term on an unused path.

Stage 2 freezes Stage 1 globals and fits per-clip bias plus the dense-grid
shared $(\theta_r,\nu_r)$ path as a conditional MAP diagnostic under one exact
OU state prior. The latent path is integrated inside every moving-frame atom
(§4.2), on a state grid chosen by the phase-dynamics bandwidth (§4.4). The
independent residual phase is **integrated out analytically** through
$\exp(-D_g|\tau|)$ in the conditional expected periodogram. There is no EM, no
Kalman filter, no particle method, no per-harmonic $\epsilon$ latent inference
and no dense smoother.

The exact discrete-time shaft transition is retained here because Stage 2 uses
it as the state prior and the renderer advances the same process. For time
interval $\Delta$,

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\theta_{r,n+1}\\
\nu_{r,n+1}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & (1-a)/\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\\
0 & a
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
\theta_{r,n}\\
\nu_{r,n}
\end{bmatrix}
+q_{r,n},
\qquad
a=e^{-\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\Delta}.
$$

The harmonic residual transition,

$$
\epsilon_{rk,n+1}
:=\epsilon_{rk,n}
+\sqrt{2D_g\Delta}\,\xi_{rk,n},
$$

started from uniform initial residual phases (§2.3), is the **renderer**
transition. It is what the optional smoother stack of Stage 4 would treat as a
latent state, but it is **not** a latent path C2 infers.

## Stage 4: optional future — joint latent-state smoothing

For each overlap group, the complex observations could be fitted jointly, with
rotor state $s_{r,n}=(\theta_{r,n},\nu_{r,n})$ and one residual state
$\epsilon_{rk,n}$ per included order, by MAP smoothing with iterative
linearisation:

1. initialize phases from isolated regions on both sides of the crossing;
2. optimize phase increments rather than unconstrained absolute phases;
3. linearize the complex observations around the current trajectory;
4. solve the sparse Gaussian smoothing problem;
5. update the nonlinear phases and repeat;
6. damp, or use Levenberg--Marquardt, when a step crosses a phase branch;
7. compute a Laplace covariance around the final MAP solution.

This is an iterated extended Kalman smoother in spirit, and it is
**approximate**: the complex exponential makes the smoothing law non-Gaussian,
so only the linear conditional amplitude solve and the exact Gaussian state
transitions are exact. If it is ever implemented it must be validated against a
dense small-$K$ reference on objective value and recovery, and only **measured**
scaling may be quoted (§12).

## Stage 5: optional future — amplitude updates by conditional linear fitting

Conditional on the phase trajectories and fixed spatial signatures, many
amplitude parameters enter linearly, which invites variable projection or
alternating optimization: smooth the phases with amplitudes held fixed, solve
regularised complex least squares for the amplitudes with the phases held
fixed, update the slow amplitude hyperparameters, and repeat. Constrain source
amplitudes to be non-negative once the spatial phase convention is fixed, and
apply temporal smoothness or the existing speed law; without that, crossing
components can exchange arbitrary complex amplitude and phase. C2 updates these
blocks inside Stage 1's marginal objective.

## Stage 6: optional future — dynamic hyperparameter updates

$\lambda_r$, $\sigma_{\nu,r}$ and the diffusion could be updated from expected
transition sufficient statistics in an approximate generalized-EM loop —
E-step: smooth the latent shaft and harmonic phases; M-step: update dynamics,
amplitudes, spatial parameters and observation covariance. Keep informative
bounds early, and in particular prevent the independent diffusion from
absorbing all shared shaft motion before the model has a stable carrier
explanation. C2 does none of this: it fixes $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$, fits
$\sigma_g$ and $D_g$ in the marginal Stage 1, then freezes them for the
conditional Stage 2 diagnostic.

## Stage 7: the power and floor block, inside C2 Stage 1

The average powers and the floor are refined against the frozen composite risk

$$
\mathcal{L}_c=\sum_i a_i\left[\frac{I_i}{M_i}+\log M_i\right],
$$

with positive overlap-exposure weights $a_i$ normalized per unique audio
duration, on the fixed band and fixed microphones of Stage 0. **Duplicate
identical observation windows split exposure**, keyed at **analysis-frame**
identity — `(recording, absolute frame centre, window/NFFT)` — and not at clip
span: duplicating one frame changes neither the score nor the effective
exposure. It is a **composite risk**, valid for mean prediction under arbitrary
dependence because $E[\mathcal L_i]=M_i^{*}/M_i+\log M_i$ is uniquely minimized
at $M_i=M_i^{*}$ — and it is not a joint NLL, not evidence, not a posterior and
not an independent term count. Cellwise Hessians and nominal frame counts cannot
supply uncertainty, and no percentage NLL is reported.

The objective the Stage 1 optimizer sees is this risk divided by one frozen
scalar **composite temperature** $T$. $T=J/H$ is a **scalar gain-direction
sandwich** correction, calibrated on frozen baseline predictive draws under a
fixed master seed and a preregistered draw count and support, using the **same
exposure, microphone and bin weights as the fit objective** — never the
per-unique-second normalized reporting form of the score above; exposure
bookkeeping and the fit temperature are different knobs. It calibrates **one
direction only**: it does not make the composite a likelihood and gives no
posterior curvature or uncertainty for any other parameter. It is frozen before
any candidate is fitted and never retuned afterwards, and a non-positive or
non-finite $J$ is a loud calibration failure, never a fallback to $T=1$.
Definition, derivation and the full constraint list:
`bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd` §6.2.4. Baseline calibration has completed:
$T=5.19201722008$ for DREGON cruise and $T=15.214066879865468$ for Michael's
rig, with Michael's repaired ramp LTAS baseline 4.851130861625892 dB against a
pooled null tolerance of 0.0788731273157346 dB. C2 real fitting/evaluation is
authorized and running elsewhere; no result is reported here.

A multichannel form is available where spatial covariance matters,

$$
\mathbf\Sigma_Y(n,q)
=\mathbf\Sigma_F(n,q)
+\sum_{r,k}
P_{rk,n}Q_{rk,nq}
\mathbf h_{rk,q}\mathbf h_{rk,q}^H,
$$

whose kernel $Q_{rk,nq}$ must contain the physical phase correlation, the
telemetry motion inside the frame, and the analysis window. It too is a
composite: shared phase and window overlap create dependencies that a
cell-independent objective omits, and a dense Gaussian likelihood over a
redundant complete STFT array is singular (§4.4).

## Stage 8: optional future — full joint refinement

Refining every parameter block together, initialized from the staged solution
and retaining the priors learned on isolated regions, is optional future
complexity. If it is ever done, compare the joint and the staged solutions: a
large parameter jump is a warning about non-identifiability, not automatic
evidence of improvement.

# 8. Choice of inference algorithm

C2's default choice is ordinary Adam in two labelled stages: a marginal Stage 1
for global parameters, followed by a frozen-global conditional Stage 2 carrier
diagnostic with one exact Gaussian state prior. That is the default — not
because it is the most powerful method available, but because each stage has a
clear contract, no approximation stack is hidden, and failures are visible.

## 8.1 Optional future: an iterated Gaussian smoother

An iterated Gaussian smoother, or direct sparse MAP optimization of the latent
phase trajectories, is the natural first extension, because telemetry supplies
a strong nominal phase, the state transitions are Gaussian, the nonlinearity
sits in a smooth complex exponential, the state precision matrix is sparse in
time, most crossings are local, and a good initialization exists outside
crossings. Automatic differentiation with sparse or banded linear algebra is
appropriate, and one would optimize residual phase increments and small carrier
corrections rather than the full audio-frequency phase. It is **not** C2's
default.

## 8.2 Optional future: particle methods

A particle smoother is **not** a default under any circumstances. It would be
considered only if the posterior became meaningfully multimodal — two sources
coincident for a long interval, nearly equal spatial signatures, weak or absent
companion harmonics, telemetry uncertainty admitting several crossing
assignments, or phase uncertainty exceeding several cycles. A
Rao--Blackwellised method could then sample the few ambiguous shaft or identity
hypotheses while conditionally smoothing approximately Gaussian states. Never
begin with a particle filter over every $\epsilon_{rk}$: its dimension grows
with the number of orders, and degeneracy follows.

## 8.3 When the model is simply unidentifiable

No inference algorithm can separate two arbitrary sources that have, over a
long interval:

- identical carrier trajectories;
- identical spatial signatures;
- no visible companion harmonics;
- unconstrained amplitudes;
- independent unknown phases.

In that case report uncertainty over the allocation or represent the pair as an
unresolved group. Do not force a unique decomposition.

# 9. Handling carrier uncertainty

Carrier uncertainty must be low dimensional and shared across harmonics. The
admissible terms are:

1. one audio/telemetry delay $\delta_r$ per rotor;
2. one per-clip frequency bias $b_{c,r}$ — a random effect with a proper prior
   and a population/recording mean, not a free per-clip number;
3. one integrated-OU residual, already represented by $\theta_r$ and its
   stationary speed state $\nu_r$.

That is the whole list.

:::: {.callout-warning}
## Withdrawn: the "very smooth calibration spline"

An earlier version of this section admitted, as a fourth term, "a very smooth
calibration spline shared by all orders". **That item is deleted.** The reason
is stronger than the weak-identifiability warning it used to carry: two
time-resolved carrier paths are an exact **gauge non-identifiability**. If the
phase contains a free correction $c(t)$ together with $\dot\theta(t)=\nu(t)$,
then for any $g(t)$

$$
c'(t)=c(t)+g(t),
\qquad
\nu'(t)=\nu(t)-2\pi g(t)
$$

produces **exactly the same waveform**. No acoustic observation can split the
variation between the two paths, and a smoothness prior merely chooses an
arbitrary split. The identifiable parameterization is §2.1's, and the
per-frame carrier correction *is* the posterior $\nu_r$.

The planted check: enable both paths deliberately, verify that the Hessian has
the predicted gauge (zero or near-zero) direction, then verify that the
one-state model recovers only their planted **sum**.
::::

Telemetry may also, as an **option**, be incorporated as a noisy observation of
the actual speed,

$$
\widehat f_r(t_j)
=f_r(t_j+\delta_r)+e_{r,j},
$$

which is useful when telemetry precision and timing uncertainty are known. It
is clearly optional, it is not part of C2, and it never displaces the
raw array's role as the primary scoring reference.

# 10. Crossings and source identity

## 10.1 Prevent label switching

Rotor labels are defined by telemetry trajectories, not by instantaneous
frequency ordering. A component must not change rotor identity because one
trajectory passes another.

Maintain labels by:

- using **raw**-telemetry-derived atoms with persistent rotor identifiers;
- sharing $\theta_r$ across all orders belonging to rotor $r$, so that identity
  lives in a **shared latent state** rather than in a per-cell decision;
- summing all overlapping components continuously in the observation model, so
  that no assignment is made at all;
- holding spatial signatures smooth through crossings;
- anchoring the solution with separated observations on both sides.

C2 needs neither a group graph nor a hysteresis stack for this (§6). A crossing
is simply an interval in which two components of the same continuous sum
coincide in frequency; unresolved overlaps are **excluded from moment
diagnostics** rather than allocated, and no allocation is forced when a pair is
unidentifiable.

## 10.2 Use all harmonic evidence

Suppose order $k$ of rotor 1 crosses order $l$ of rotor 2. The ambiguous pair
should inherit shaft estimates from other visible orders:

$$
\theta_1(t)
\leftarrow
\{\psi_{1j}(t)/j:j\ne k\},
$$

$$
\theta_2(t)
\leftarrow
\{\psi_{2j}(t)/j:j\ne l\}.
$$

The crossing then becomes mainly an inference problem for the two independent
residuals and amplitudes, rather than for two completely unknown phases.

## 10.3 Do not ignore interference

Expected powers from independent sources add after ensemble averaging. A single
recording contains complex interference:

$$
|X_1+X_2|^2
=|X_1|^2+|X_2|^2
+2\operatorname{Re}(X_1X_2^*).
$$

A power-only likelihood treats the last term as unexplained variation. Near a
crossing it can bias amplitude and linewidth estimates. The complex observation
likelihood represents it directly.

# 11. Regularisation

The following priors or penalties are recommended.

## 11.1 Dynamics

- C2: fixed $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, fitted positive
  $\sigma_g$ and one scalar $D_g$ per rig, Stage 1 marginal fit followed by
  frozen-global Stage 2 diagnostic carrier inference;
- one recording-level gain shared across regimes, and a per-clip bias with a
  proper prior — a free per-clip or per-regime level can absorb the entire
  speed law, and a zero-mean per-clip nuisance alone does not fix slope
  confounding unless it is orthogonal to log-speed;
- separate between-recording variation from within-recording stochastic state;
- optional future only: per-order $D_{rk}$, hierarchical smoothness of
  $\log D_{rk}$ over $\log k$, and partial pooling of dynamics across rotors
  where bench evidence supports it.

## 11.2 Amplitudes

- the existing speed-dependent power law;
- slow temporal amplitude variation;
- shrinkage for weak or absent harmonics;
- no abrupt amplitude exchange at crossings.

## 11.3 Spatial responses

- fixed normalization and phase convention;
- smoothness over nearby frequencies;
- weak variation over time unless microphone or rotor geometry changes;
- uncertainty propagated from clean-region estimation.

## 11.4 Floor

- smooth spectral covariance;
- positive-definite multichannel covariance parameterization;
- estimation from line-free regions where possible;
- no freedom to create narrow moving features that imitate harmonics.

# 12. Computational structure

The implementation should exploit four forms of sparsity.

1. **Frequency sparsity.** Each harmonic affects only a narrow band.
2. **Crossing sparsity.** Most lines are isolated most of the time.
3. **Temporal Markov sparsity.** State priors connect adjacent times.
4. **Rotor sparsity.** Harmonics couple through only four shaft states.

A practical batch can contain:

- one time interval;
- all four shaft states for that interval;
- all reliable non-crossing harmonic summaries;
- full complex observations only for active overlap groups.

Use blockwise smoothing with overlap longer than the largest fitted correlation
time. Reconcile adjacent blocks through shared boundary-state distributions,
not by resetting phases independently.

No complexity claim in this document is a theorem. In particular there is **no
exact $O(K)$ structured-Kalman result**: conditioning on the shaft angle
induces residual correlations between orders that a recursion does not remove,
so rank-one-plus-diagonal structure at one step does not survive recursive
conditioning (companion explainer §6.1.6). Quote **measured** scaling only.
C2 sidesteps the question entirely: it runs ordinary Adam on one
objective with batched FFTs, and its cost is whatever it is measured to be.

# 13. Validation on planted data

The crossing problem requires dedicated simulations. Static single-comb round
trips are not sufficient.

The canonical correctness list — the checks required before any fit of this
family is believed — is §9 of `bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd`, and it
governs here too: exact integrated-OU moments including the near-zero
$\lambda\Delta$ limit, with correlated $\theta$/$\nu$ increments from one
shared state; shaft-only, independent-only and combined planted phase
covariance with its $k$ loading and order-normalised differences, plus the
deliberate two-path Hessian gauge check of §9; conditional-versus-marginal
collapse as $C_{\text{post}}\to0$, with $D=0$ MAP-path recovery and
$\theta=0$ scalar-$D$ recovery; finite-window power for a pure tone and a
planted chirp including fractional bins, floor and phase units; the
subwindow-oscillation line and **state-grid convergence as
$\Delta_{\text{state}}$ shrinks at fixed STFT hop and window**; overlap
duplicates creating no exposure and no held-out raw-sample leakage; the
rendered physical RPS integrating to the shared phase, excluding $\epsilon$,
and matching the audio timeline and length after resampling; near-crossing
behaviour on the continuously summed spectral components that share the same
$\theta$, with the companion harmonics of both rotors, no nearest-bin
classification and no forced unidentifiable allocation — a **joint complex
observation** crossing check belongs to the optional $\epsilon$-latent /
state-space stack (Stage 4, §8.1) and to a future candidate that implements
that likelihood, not to C2, which integrates out $\epsilon$ in the production
candidate; finite parameter and device gradients; and — only if a sparse method
is ever introduced — a small-$K$ comparison against a dense reference on
objective and recovery, with no exact-$O(K)$ assertion.

The crossing-specific cases below are additional to that list. They are
diagnostics, not gates.

## 13.1 Required planted cases

1. Four separated combs with known dynamic parameters.
2. One pairwise crossing with different spatial signatures.
3. One pairwise crossing with one microphone only.
4. Several simultaneous crossings involving different orders.
5. Nearly parallel trajectories that remain close for a long interval.
6. A missing companion-harmonic interval.
7. Telemetry delay and bias.
8. Low-SNR high orders.
9. Equal shaft parameters but different $D_{rk}$.
10. A deliberate shared cross-rotor disturbance.

## 13.2 Metrics

Measure more than reconstruction error:

- carrier-delay and bias recovery;
- $\lambda_r$ and $\sigma_{\nu,r}$ recovery;
- $D_{rk}$ recovery;
- shaft trajectory error modulo global phase;
- phase-increment covariance calibration;
- source allocation through crossings;
- amplitude bias before, during, and after crossings;
- uncertainty coverage;
- multichannel spectral fit;
- round-trip renderer recovery;
- downstream rotor-tracker error.

## 13.3 Crossing-specific acceptance rule

A fit passes a crossing test only if rotor identity remains consistent across
the crossing and uncertainty increases when the sources are weakly
identifiable. A visually smooth but overconfident arbitrary allocation is a
failure.

# 14. Validation on real data

Use the following hierarchy of evidence.

1. **Non-crossing phase covariance:** does every rotor show its predicted
   rank-one order loading?
2. **Order-normalised differences:** does shaft motion cancel?
3. **Crossing prediction:** parameters learned outside crossings must predict
   the held-out crossings' observed periodograms through the continuously
   summed spectral components. Predicting the **complex** observations inside
   a crossing is the future $\epsilon$-latent candidate's test, not C2's.
4. **Multiple microphones:** do spatial signatures learned outside crossings
   remain valid inside them?
5. **Multiple window lengths:** do physical parameters stay fixed when the
   observation window changes?
6. **Posterior predictive audio:** do generated recordings reproduce phase,
   spectral, and amplitude statistics?
7. **Downstream transfer:** does the fitted renderer improve blind flight
   tracker behaviour, as read by the frozen gates?

Hold out contiguous intervals containing complete crossings, behind a
window/filter-length support guard so that no raw-sample support leaks.
Randomly holding out overlapping STFT cells leaks information and gives an
optimistic result.

The frozen protocol these checks run under is recorded in
`docs/experiments/revised-phase-campaign.qmd` and is not negotiable here:

- **DREGON: cruise only.** The five independently recorded no-source room2
  cruise recordings are the clustered units. There is no standby or ramp
  acceptance for this rig, and DREGON standby/ramp need not be fitted at all.
- **Michael's rig:** fit on FLY125 — standby, ramp and cruise under **one**
  joint parameter law per rig, never independent per-regime vectors, with one
  recording-level gain shared across regimes. **FLY124 stays held out**, and
  every uncertainty statement about it is explicitly conditional on that one
  recording.
- **Reference agreement, not ground truth.** The primary tracker score uses
  the **same raw telemetry array** for the real arm and for every synthetic
  arm. Refined and posterior tracks are fit provenance and diagnostics only;
  the renderer's realized shaft label supplies a diagnostic MAE.
- **Held-out predictive synthesis** uses only raw held-out telemetry, the
  training-derived bias law, and **one fresh OU draw** — no refined labels and
  no corrections inferred from the held-out audio.
- Do not mix physical rigs or bench cells into flight data. Bench is an
  optional planted/physical diagnostic, not a reported scientific candidate
  arm.

# 15. Baselines

Compare the proposed fit with at least these baselines:

| Baseline | Question answered |
|---|---|
| Nearest-trajectory bin assignment | How much is gained by joint crossing inference? |
| Independent moving Lorentzian lines | How much is gained by shared phase dynamics? |
| Independent two-Cauchy lines | How much is gained over a flexible marginal spectrum? |
| Joint multichannel spectral model without latent phase | How much is gained by complex temporal smoothing? |
| Shared-shaft plus independent-residual model | The proposed mechanism; C2 is the current fixed-reference implementation |

Old exports are **rescored, never refitted**, under an identical observation
and renderer protocol, using their **stated** covariance and their **actual
exported units**. A smoothed observed periodogram is not a model prediction.

The proposed model need not win every marginal spectral score. Its reason for
existence is to explain both marginal line shapes and joint phase behaviour
with one renderable physical mechanism — and acceptance is decided by the
frozen gates, not by this descriptive ladder.

# 16. Common failure modes

## Identity swaps

**Symptom:** fitted amplitudes or spatial vectors exchange rotor labels at a
crossing.

**Response:** strengthen temporal continuity, use companion harmonics, extend
the smoothing interval, and fix rotor identity to telemetry rather than
frequency rank.

## Harmonic residual absorbs shaft motion

**Symptom:** $D_{rk}$ becomes large and cross-order covariance is underfit.

**Response:** initialize shaft parameters from off-diagonal covariance and
regularise $D_{rk}$ hierarchically.

## Shaft process absorbs telemetry misalignment

**Symptom:** apparent shaft variance grows during acceleration and is correlated
with $d\widehat f_r/dt$.

**Response:** fit telemetry/audio delay before stochastic dynamics.

## Amplitudes steal phase mismatch

**Symptom:** amplitudes fluctuate rapidly or exchange power at crossings.

**Response:** use complex observations, constrain amplitude smoothness, and fix
the spatial phase convention.

## Spatial response absorbs source identity

**Symptom:** $\mathbf h_{rk}$ changes abruptly only during overlaps.

**Response:** learn it away from crossings and keep it fixed or strongly
regularised during joint inference.

## Overconfident decomposition

**Symptom:** the method reports precise individual sources during a prolonged
unidentifiable collision.

**Response:** inspect posterior curvature, allow unresolved groups, and report
allocation uncertainty.

## Two carrier paths at once

**Symptom:** a fitted smooth carrier correction and a fitted shaft path are
individually large and nearly cancel, and the split moves when the smoothness
prior moves.

**Response:** there is only one time-resolved carrier state (§9). Remove the
second path; the per-frame correction *is* the posterior $\nu_r$.

## The posterior path multiplied by the prior linewidth

**Symptom:** a conditional reconstruction stays broad even when the shaft path
is essentially known.

**Response:** choose the branch once. With $C_{\text{post}}\to0$ the
conditional spectrum must collapse to the deterministic windowed moving atom
apart from $\epsilon$; any residual OU broadening is a double count.

## A frame-centre residual phase

**Symptom:** ramps fit worse than steady segments, and the misfit scales with
the within-frame frequency excursion.

**Response:** integrate the latent path inside every moving-frame atom (§4.2).
Overlapping frames do not recover subwindow dynamics.

## Duplicate windows counted as evidence

**Symptom:** the score, or its uncertainty, improves when the same observation
window is included twice.

**Response:** overlap-exposure weights must **split** exposure across
duplicate windows. The score and the effective exposure are invariant to
duplication.

# 17. C2: the concrete round-2 implementation

C2 is the current implemented member of this family. Its pipeline is the
candidate list of §1; this section states the interface it exposes and the
evidence it must carry. It has passed remote preflight, but no real DREGON or
Michael gate result is reported here.

## 17.1 Public API surface

Four entry points, agreed before code:

- `fit_revised(...)` — produces the fit export.
- `predict_spectrum(export, clip, *, n_fft, hop)` — the expected periodogram,
  shaped to match the data's own periodogram. The held-out path is raw-only
  and optimizes nothing on that clip's audio.
- `render_revised(export, rps, *, sample_rate, sample_rate_native, n_mics, seed)`
  — audio, plus the realized interval-average shaft label and the
  `reference_rps`, under the renderer contract of the companion explainer.
- `infer_carrier(export, clip, ...)` — the diagnostic posterior track, never
  invoked implicitly inside prediction or rendering.

Both expected-PSD adapters — the marginal branch and the conditional plug-in
branch — share **one** finite-window convention. Stored training MAP paths are
**diagnostics**: they are never a default predictive input for a new clip.

## 17.2 Export schema

The export records `schema_version`, `model_family='shared_shaft_ou'`,
`fit_method='marginal_then_carrier'`, `lambda_source='fixed_reference'`,
`rig_id`, the physical parameters (delay, the per-clip bias law, fixed
$\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$, fitted $\sigma_g$, the scalar $D_g$, line and floor
powers, the tied speed law, the microphone response), the training provenance
(dataset pins, recordings, supports, seeds, and the label key actually used),
and the fit diagnostics including the training-only state posterior.

## 17.3 Driver

```
python scripts/stochastic_fit_revised.py \
  --manifest <frozen-manifest> --rig <michaels|dregon|bench> \
  --device cuda --out <path>
```

The manifest is frozen **before** any fit; the gate runner is a separate
script owned by the evaluation worker. The implementation of these files
belongs to the candidate-implementation worker — this document specifies the
science and the interface, not the file contents.

## 17.4 The route to a trustworthy prototype

1. Integrate **raw** telemetry with a phase-continuous interpolator.
2. Estimate one delay and one per-clip bias for each rotor.
3. Extract complex raw-telemetry-demodulated harmonic subbands for diagnostics.
4. Run moment diagnostics only; do not use them to set production
   hyperparameters.
5. Fix $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
6. Fit Stage 1's marginal expected-periodogram objective for $\sigma_g,D_g$,
   powers, floor, speed law and bias parameters.
7. Freeze those globals and fit Stage 2's conditional carrier diagnostic path.
8. Run the planted checks of §13 and the frozen evaluation runner; report real
   fit/gate numbers only after they exist.

# 18. Final recommendation

The main inference object is the latent rotor state, not the fitted width of
each spectral line.

For four moving combs, the strategy actually recommended — C2 — is

$$
\boxed{
\begin{array}{c}
\text{raw telemetry}+\text{delay}+\text{per-clip bias}
\\[0.2em]
+\text{fixed }\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}+\text{fitted }\sigma_g,D_g
\\[0.2em]
+\text{Stage 1 marginal expected-periodogram fit}
\\[0.2em]
+\text{Stage 2 frozen-global conditional carrier diagnostic}
\end{array}
}
$$

The general stack of this document — overlap graphs, temporal hysteresis,
complex state smoothing, EM, particle methods — is held in reserve as optional
future complexity, admitted one step at a time and only when a **named**
acceptance criterion has actually failed.

The other harmonics of each rotor are not merely additional lines to fit. They
are repeated measurements of the same shaft trajectory. That shared latent
state is what makes separation through crossings possible — and in C2 it is
realised simply by summing every component continuously, never by assigning one.
